nodes.title: Open-world terrain tiles (read me first)
widgets_values:
A 2 km × 2 km open-world terrain delivered as 4 × 4 tiles, engine-agnostic:
  · Height: 1025² samples, 2 m per cell; each tile a 257² 16-bit PNG, **neighbouring tiles share the row of pixels on their common edge** (heights at the seams are bit-identical when stitched); metres = minimum + value × range, the range is in Height.json's range_scaled (one range for the whole map, the same for all tiles). A full-map .r16 is included too.
  · Weight maps: six layers Grass / ForestFloor / Sediment / Rock / Snow / Water, one 8-bit greyscale PNG per tile per layer, **summing to 1 everywhere** (usable directly as the engine's terrain layers).
  · Instances: trees (3 pine and 2 broadleaf kinds, split by altitude), bushes, rocks (asset names match the SM_Rock_0N exported by the rock pipeline), written as CSV in 512 m tiles, plus Instances_index.json listing each tile.

Coordinate convention (written into every .json): origin at the north-west corner = top left of the height map, x east, z south (matching image row order), y up, units in metres. Instance transforms are read the same way as Copy to Points, so what the preview places is what the table says.

① Terrain, erode → upres → erode (the Houdini way): a massif belt is grown at 513² by Stream Power (rivers cut the uplifted ground: branching ridges, spurs and valleys) → lowland restored, concave mountain profiles → HeightField Erode at 513² (rain, flowing water, sediment) → resize to 1025² → gully pattern (erosion filter, on the massif only) → HeightField Erode at 1025², which also writes the flow, sediment and debris masks → flow accumulation (rivers, lakes) → Splat Map. About two minutes on numpy, much less with CUDA.
② Ecology and colour from the erosion masks: rock darkened where water streaks down it, light scree on the debris, alluvium (grassed where thin) on the sediment, lush grass where water collects; forest in clumps below a ragged tree line, bigger trees where it is wet, bushes on forest edges and alpine ledges, rocks on scree.
③ Distribution: each of the three instance kinds scatters by its density map, samples height, picks an asset and sets orientation (trees upright with random rotation, rocks tilted a bit towards the slope).
④ Write files + preview: the full-map mesh with instance proxies (stacked-cone pines, clustered broadleaf crowns, bushes, rocks), shot from a Camera node over the lowlands toward the range in the Outdoor look (side-lit sun, haze).

# lowland: gentle rolling relief tilted toward the south-west so the plains drain instead of pooling
low = 0.02 * (@C - 0.5) + 0.012 * (@u + 1 - @v)
# massif: a low-frequency belt. It is NOT drawn as mountains here -- Stream Power uplifts it and rivers cut it,
# which is what gives ridges, spurs and valleys their branching (ridged noise only imitates that).
# The belt runs north-west to south-east across the north-east half (across the camera's view), with a
# wandering axis, saddles and summits along it, plus a few foothill knolls; it fades out before the map edges
# (the edges are the rivers' base level: uplift there would stand up as walls)
ax = (@u + @v - 1.3 + 0.4 * (noise(set(@u * 1.6 - @v * 1.6, 0.5, 7.3)) - 0.5)) * 0.7071
belt = 1 - smoothstep(0.06, 0.30, abs(ax))
belt = belt * (0.4 + 0.8 * noise(set((@u - @v) * 2.2, 1.5, 5.1)))
knoll = 0.35 * smoothstep(0.56, 0.74, noise(set(@u * 3.2, @v * 3.2, 9.4)))
edge = smoothstep(0.02, 0.14, min(min(@u, 1 - @u), min(@v, 1 - @v)))
m = clamp(max(belt, knoll), 0, 1) * edge
@m = m
@base = low
# the massif starts as noisy high ground (irregular summits and shoulders); the rivers then cut it
@C = low + m * (0.05 + 0.10 * @C * @C)
nodes.title: Lowland + massif mask

widgets_values:
# Stream Power fills every pit before it starts, which flattens the lowland into plains; outside the massif
# the original rolling relief comes back
k = smoothstep(0.1, 0.7, @m)
@C = lerp(@base, @C, k)
# slightly concave profiles: steeper toward the crests, long aprons at the foot
top = @C.max()
r = clamp((@C - @base) / (top - @base), 0, 1)
@C = @base + (top - @base) * pow(r, 1.25)

# what the erosion left lying around: slumped scree (debris) and water-laid sediment, in height values
@loose = @debris + @sediment
nodes.title: Loose material (scree + alluvium)

widgets_values:
hn = (@C - @C.min()) / (@C.max() - @C.min())
@hn = hn
# terrain normal to world space (image x → world +X, image y (north) → world −Z, z → +Y)
@tn = normalize(set(@N.x, @N.z, -@N.y))
steep = 1 - @N.z
wet = clamp(@flow, 0, 1)
# forest: where soil holds (not rock, not scree, not water), below a ragged tree line, on slopes under ~35°,
# thicker where water collects. Two scales of patches give clumps with edges and clearings, not an even carpet
# thin alluvium grows grass and trees too; only the scree stays bare
scree_f = smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, @debris / (@loose + 1e-9))
soil = (@splat_grass + 0.8 * @splat_sediment * (1 - scree_f)) * (1 - smoothstep(0.14, 0.24, steep))
tl = 0.62 + 0.12 * (noise(set(@u * 7, @v * 7, 8.8)) - 0.5) + 0.06 * wet
below = 1 - smoothstep(-0.06, 0.02, hn - tl)
big = smoothstep(0.36, 0.56, noise(set(@u * 5, @v * 5, 1.7)) + 0.35 * wet)
small = smoothstep(0.3, 0.6, noise(set(@u * 28, @v * 28, 4.2)))
f = clamp(soil * below * big * (0.55 + 0.45 * small), 0, 1)
veg = 0.8 * @splat_sediment * (1 - scree_f)
@Grass = (@splat_grass + veg) * (1 - f)
@ForestFloor = (@splat_grass + veg) * f
@Sediment = @splat_sediment - veg
@Rock = @splat_rock
@Snow = @splat_snow
@Water = @splat_water
# scatter densities: forest; lone trees in meadows; bushes along forest edges and on wet ground and alpine
# ledges; rocks on scree and at the foot of cliffs
@d_tree = @ForestFloor + 0.04 * @Grass * below
edge_ = f * (1 - f) * 4
@d_bush = @Grass * (0.25 * edge_ + 0.35 * wet + 0.5 * smoothstep(0.5, 0.7, hn) * (1 - smoothstep(0.2, 0.35, steep))) * smoothstep(0.35, 0.65, noise(set(@u * 23, @v * 23, 5.3)))
@d_rock = 0.35 * smoothstep(0.0005, 0.003, @debris) + 0.3 * smoothstep(0.2, 0.5, @Rock) * (1 - 0.6 * @Rock) + 0.15 * @Sediment
@wet = wet
# colour (display values, made linear at the end). Rock: warm and cool greys in patches, faint irregular
# bedding (about 9 m, warped -- smooth bands, never a step), darker where water streaks down it, lighter scree
# below. Grass: lush where wet, dry and yellow on ridges and high meadows
rv = noise(set(@u * 9, @v * 9, 2.6))
bed = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(@C * 2048 / 9 + 8 * noise(set(@u * 3, @v * 3, 6.1)))
rock = lerp(set(0.38, 0.35, 0.31), set(0.62, 0.60, 0.56), rv) * (0.86 + 0.2 * bed)
rock = rock * (0.9 + 0.2 * hn)
# lichen and thin soil on the gentler rock
rock = lerp(rock, set(0.36, 0.38, 0.27), 0.5 * (1 - smoothstep(0.2, 0.4, steep)) * noise(set(@u * 30, @v * 30, 6.6)))
# water streaks: dark down the gullies, staining the faces below
rock = rock * (1 - 0.5 * smoothstep(0.3, 0.9, wet))
scree = set(0.60, 0.57, 0.52) * (0.9 + 0.2 * noise(set(@u * 80, @v * 80, 3.9)))
alluv = lerp(set(0.36, 0.38, 0.24), set(0.52, 0.48, 0.38), smoothstep(0.002, 0.006, @sediment))
loose = lerp(alluv, scree, scree_f)
dry = clamp(smoothstep(0.35, 0.75, noise(set(@u * 6, @v * 6, 4.4))) * 0.7 + 0.5 * hn - 0.8 * wet, 0, 1)
grass = lerp(set(0.23, 0.31, 0.12), set(0.44, 0.44, 0.22), dry)
# alpine meadow above the tree line: paler, olive
grass = lerp(grass, set(0.42, 0.45, 0.27), smoothstep(-0.05, 0.1, hn - tl))
grass = grass * (0.9 + 0.2 * noise(set(@u * 40, @v * 40, 7.7)))
c = (grass * @Grass + set(0.17, 0.22, 0.10) * @ForestFloor + loose * @Sediment + rock * @Rock + set(0.90, 0.91, 0.94) * @Snow + set(0.05, 0.11, 0.13) * @Water)
@albedo = (c * (0.94 + 0.12 * noise(set(@u * 120, @v * 120, 2.2)))) ** 2.2
# for the preview: ambient occlusion 1, roughness (water is a mirror, wet rock glistens a little), metallic 0
@terrain_orm = set(1 + 0 * hn, lerp(0.92 - 0.25 * wet * @Rock, 0.04, @Water), 0 * hn)
nodes.title: Ecology: six weight layers + scatter densities

widgets_values:
r = rand(@ptnum + 0.5)
pine = np.array(["Tree_Pine_A", "Tree_Pine_B", "Tree_Pine_C"])
broad = np.array(["Tree_Broadleaf_A", "Tree_Broadleaf_B"])
# pines up high, broadleaf down low, a mixed band in between (by altitude + random)
high = @hn.x + 0.1 * (rand(@ptnum + 7.1) - 0.5) > 0.3
s@name = where(high, pine[(r * 3).astype(int)], broad[(r * 2).astype(int)])
a = rand(@ptnum + 1.3) * 2 * PI
@N = set(sin(a), 0 * a, cos(a))
@up = set(0, 1, 0)
# big trees deep in the forest and where water collects, smaller at the edges and up toward the tree line
d = clamp(@d_tree.x, 0, 1)
@pscale = (0.75 + 0.5 * d + 0.4 * @wet.x) * (1 - 0.4 * smoothstep(0.45, 0.65, @hn.x)) * (0.7 + 0.6 * rand(@ptnum + 2.9))
